results.title: CT image quality assessment - an in-depth review - Springer Nature
results.content: The development of CT-IQA can be divided into three distinct phases: (1) Subjective Assessment Dominance Period (1990-2000): Early stage evaluations relied primarily on radiologists’ expertise, with outcomes constrained by individual variability and time-intensive workflows; (2) Emergence of Objective Algorithms (2000-2015): Advances in computing technology and digital image processing facilitated standardized assessments through pixel statistics, information theory, structural feature-based algorithms, and quantitative metrics for imaging systems, although these methods suffered from high computational complexity and limited correlation with human visual perception; (3) Artificial intelligence (AI)-Driven Innovation Era (2016-present): Deep learning models have demonstrated potential in artifact correction and low-dose imaging optimization, while confronting challenges in generalizability, model explainability, and ethical debates regarding clinical deployment.
